legalName: Petition for Expungement of Non-Conviction Records Pursuant to Pa.R.Crim.P. 790
publicName: Expunge a Pennsylvania court case that did not end in a conviction
mechanism: Section 9122(a) requires expungement of criminal history record information where no disposition has been received or recorded within 18 months after the date of arrest and the court finds the conditions met, or where a court order requires nonconviction data to be expunged. Rule 790 prescribes the petition contents, the attached Pennsylvania State Police criminal history report, service on the attorney for the Commonwealth, and the expungement order for court cases.
exclusions: Mixed cases in which any charge in the case resulted in a conviction. Section 9122(a) reaches nonconviction data; a case with a conviction on any count is not a clean non-conviction.
Cases in which only summary offenses were filed and the case remained at the magisterial district court, which proceed under Pa.R.Crim.P. 490 instead.
Records held by federal, military, tribal or out-of-state authorities, which Pennsylvania relief does not reach.

Arrest with no disposition received or recorded
waitingPeriods.duration: 18 months after the date of arrest, per 18 Pa.C.S. § 9122(a)

venue: The clerk of the courts of the judicial district in which the charges were disposed. Statewide rules and forms; county instruction packets and filing fees vary.

destination.name: Clerk of the courts of the judicial district in which the charges were disposed
destination.detail: File the Rule 790 petition and blank expungement order with the clerk of courts. A copy of the petition is served on the attorney for the Commonwealth concurrently with filing. The Commonwealth has 60 days after service to file a consent or objection or take no action.

components.conditionDescription: Applies only where the participant seeks to proceed in forma pauperis.

participantActionRequired.description: Obtain Pennsylvania State Police criminal history report obtained within 60 days before filing. Request your own criminal history report from the Pennsylvania State Police. Rule 790 requires a current copy obtained within 60 days before filing to be attached, unless the attorney for the Commonwealth agrees to waive it. Because of the 60-day window, order it late in packet assembly rather than first. LegalEase never collects, inspects or authenticates it.

Obtain Complete docket sheet for the case. Obtain the docket sheet showing every charge, the OTN, and the disposition of each count.

In forma pauperis relief is available; the Court of Common Pleas Motion to Proceed In Forma Pauperis is published statewide.

provenance.sourceStatement: expungement removes the information so there is no trace or indication it existed, subject to limited data retained under § 9122(c). Limited access, including Clean Slate, seals the record from public view but leaves it available to criminal justice agencies and certain government and noncriminal justice agencies.
